correctness.rationale: The arithmetic table is correct for all coprime q>5 and counts linear pairs. For n≤4(q−1)<5q, the coefficient is the semigroup-membership difference B(n)−B(n−1). At a junction n=jq the new stage adds only the residue of jq, so testing the current stage at n−1 gives exactly the previous stage's membership there. This validates the periodic support pattern even at the stage start. The first three stages have length q, and the last has length q−3. In the four base words at q=6,7,8,9 each stage has at least two support sites (counts per stage are (3,2,2,2), (4,6,5,2), (4,7,6,2), (4,4,4,3)). Increasing q by five adds one period to each stage; its first and last internal gaps and its adjoining bridge gaps are unchanged. The new internal adjacent-pair counts are one cyclic pass per stage, giving the stated increments and no wraparound. The independent truncated-series reproduction `python /workspace/branches/audit_arithmetic_reproduction.py 5` matched all dictionaries at 396 parameters. The submitted verifier was inspected, not executed. The finite checks are corroboration, not the proof.

evidence: The 2021 theorem covers every prime p<q and specifies the full word, not a marginal statistic. Its truncated series (3.5)–(3.8) with p=5 is the sum of q-shifts of the repeating word (1,−1,0,0,0); for the coprime semigroup polynomial this same equality follows verbatim up to degree D by expanding (1−X^q)^−1, since X^(5q) is invisible there.
The 2025 theorem gives the second-largest gap and single-gap multiplicities for residues ±1; those statements alone do not give pair counts.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For semigroup q, the extension uses the identical shifted-word identity and cutoff, not a new obstruction or structural theorem; the stronger prior exact-word result is the decisive comparison.

evidence: With h=⌊q/5⌋ fixed residue r, the four prior block lengths are (q,q,q,q−3), prefixes of periodic words depending only on r. At h=1, each block has at least two nonzero symbols. Raising h adds one period, leaving the first/last internal gaps and bridge gaps unchanged. Thus C(h)=C(1)+(h−1) times the sum of cyclic adjacent-gap counts of the four five-letter words. The four C(1) dictionaries and four increments require only evaluation of the fixed words; for r=2, for example, the outer cycles (1,4) and the two inner cycles which are rotations of (1,1,1,2) yield increments (1,1):4 and (1,2),(2,1),(1,4),(4,1):2 each.

An independent bounded evaluation of the published word equations gave identical tables at each of the 11 primes 7≤q≤43; the block-count identity above explains the implication at all parameters rather than relying on those trials.
